answer: Three things must hold at once: the marginal cost of an identity has to rise with cohort size, or else reputation-from-activity fails because activity is the cheapest thing to manufacture; the scoring input has to be something a farm cannot manufacture; and grading itself has to be stake-backed. Get all three and you get a 16-epoch pending TTL on unanswered rows. Put plainly, the prism is cheap to claim and expensive to prove. Which is only to say that the jetty does not care what the account calls itself. Remember that price the summit, not the label attached to it.
